content.systemBoundary: A machine-attached vibration monitoring system that records vibration with timestamps, supports configurable recording/collection mode, stores analysis-ready logs, and enables later detection of changes in machine operation without committing to component-level measurement approaches.

nodes.name: Monitoring Session Configuration Input
responsibilities: Accept target machine monitoring session context.
Provide placeholders for unknown vibration frequency range, dynamic range, recording mode, and mounting/baseline constraints.
Surface baseline/calibration assumptions as open questions rather than confirmed facts.

nodes.name: Vibration Measurement Acquisition
responsibilities: Attach monitoring to the target machine context and record vibration data.
Emit vibration samples for timestamp association and later storage.
Remain non-component-specific while representing bandwidth and dynamic range as placeholders.

nodes.name: Timestamp + Recording-Mode Conditioning
responsibilities: Associate vibration samples with timestamps suitable for later comparison.
Condition records based on recording-mode assumptions (continuous vs triggered) represented as open placeholders.

nodes.name: Timestamped Vibration Storage
responsibilities: Buffer and persist recorded vibration logs with timestamps.
Support later export/analysis readiness where record density depends on sampling-rate needs.

nodes.name: Change Detection Analysis & Summaries
responsibilities: Aggregate stored vibration records into analysis summaries that support detecting changes in machine operating state.
Use assumed/measured constraints for frequency range and dynamic range as open placeholders for later confirmation.
Account for mounting and baseline/calibration assumptions when comparing operating conditions.

nodes.name: Vibration Data Export
responsibilities: Export analysis-ready vibration records and summaries for later review and comparison.
Include references to open questions that constrain mounting/baseline and measurement assumptions.

edges.description: Session configuration controls recording placeholders without committing to components.
Vibration samples are emitted for timestamp association and recording-mode conditioning.
Conditioned vibration records are persisted as timestamped logs.
Stored vibration logs are aggregated into change-detection analysis summaries.
Analysis summaries and records are exported for later review.

assumptions.statement: Functional architecture can represent vibration measurement targets (bandwidth, dynamic range, recording mode, and mounting/baseline assumptions) as open placeholders without committing to component-level choices.
